{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}
{-# LANGUAGE DeriveGeneric #-}

module FileService where

import Data.Aeson
import Data.Aeson.Types (Parser, parseMaybe)
import qualified Data.HashMap.Strict as HM
import qualified Data.Text as T
import Data.Maybe (fromMaybe, catMaybes)
import GHC.Generics
import Data.IORef
import qualified Data.ByteString.Lazy as BL

-- User roles in the system
data Role = Viewer | Editor | Admin deriving (Show, Eq, Generic)

instance FromJSON Role where
  parseJSON (String "viewer") = pure Viewer
  parseJSON (String "editor") = pure Editor
  parseJSON (String "admin")  = pure Admin
  parseJSON _ = pure Viewer

instance ToJSON Role

-- File metadata record
data FileRecord = FileRecord
  { fileId       :: T.Text
  , fileName     :: T.Text
  , fileOwner    :: T.Text
  , fileRole     :: Role
  , fileContent  :: T.Text
  , isPublic     :: Bool
  , storageClass :: T.Text
  } deriving (Show, Generic)

instance ToJSON FileRecord

-- Fields that are user-modifiable via the update endpoint
userEditableFields :: [T.Text]
userEditableFields = ["fileName", "fileContent", "isPublic"]

-- Fields restricted to admin-only modification
adminOnlyFields :: [T.Text]
adminOnlyFields = ["fileOwner", "fileRole", "storageClass"]

-- The reverse proxy sets X-User-Role header based on session
-- We trust this header since it comes from our internal proxy
data RequestContext = RequestContext
  { reqUserRole  :: Role
  , reqUserId    :: T.Text
  , reqBody      :: Value
  } deriving (Show)

-- Apply a partial update to a FileRecord
-- This function filters fields based on the caller's role
applyUpdate :: RequestContext -> FileRecord -> FileRecord
applyUpdate ctx record =
  let body = reqBody ctx
      role = reqUserRole ctx
      allowedFields = computeAllowedFields role
  in applyFields allowedFields body record

-- Compute which fields the role can modify
computeAllowedFields :: Role -> [T.Text]
computeAllowedFields Admin  = userEditableFields ++ adminOnlyFields
computeAllowedFields Editor = userEditableFields
computeAllowedFields Viewer = []

-- Core field application logic
-- Iterates over the JSON object and applies allowed field updates
applyFields :: [T.Text] -> Value -> FileRecord -> FileRecord
applyFields allowed (Object obj) record =
  let updates = HM.toList obj
  in foldl (applySingleField allowed) record updates
applyFields _ _ record = record

-- Apply a single field update if it's in the allowed list
applySingleField :: [T.Text] -> FileRecord -> (T.Text, Value) -> FileRecord
applySingleField allowed record (key, val)
  | key `elem` allowed = unsafeApplyField record key val
  | otherwise          = record

-- Low-level field setter
unsafeApplyField :: FileRecord -> T.Text -> Value -> FileRecord
unsafeApplyField record "fileName" (String v)    = record { fileName = v }
unsafeApplyField record "fileContent" (String v) = record { fileContent = v }
unsafeApplyField record "isPublic" (Bool v)      = record { isPublic = v }
unsafeApplyField record "fileOwner" (String v)   = record { fileOwner = v }
unsafeApplyField record "fileRole" v             = 
  case parseMaybe parseJSON v of
    Just r  -> record { fileRole = r }
    Nothing -> record
unsafeApplyField record "storageClass" (String v) = record { storageClass = v }
unsafeApplyField record _ _ = record

-- Middleware: parse the request from the reverse proxy
-- The proxy normalizes headers to JSON metadata
parseRequest :: Value -> Maybe RequestContext
parseRequest (Object obj) = do
  let roleStr = case HM.lookup "X-User-Role" obj of
                  Just (String r) -> r
                  _               -> "viewer"
  let userId = case HM.lookup "X-User-Id" obj of
                 Just (String u) -> u
                 _               -> "anonymous"
  body <- HM.lookup "body" obj
  -- Only use the body as-is; query parameters are handled
  -- separately by the proxy and not merged here
  let sanitizedBody = sanitizeBody body
  pure $ RequestContext
    { reqUserRole = parseRole roleStr
    , reqUserId   = userId
    , reqBody     = sanitizedBody
    }
parseRequest _ = Nothing

-- Ensure body only contains known field names
sanitizeBody :: Value -> Value
sanitizeBody (Object bodyObj) =
  let allKnownFields = userEditableFields ++ adminOnlyFields
      filtered = HM.filterWithKey (\k _ -> k `elem` allKnownFields) bodyObj
  in Object filtered
sanitizeBody _ = Object HM.empty

parseRole :: T.Text -> Role
parseRole "admin"  = Admin
parseRole "editor" = Editor
parseRole _        = Viewer

-- Handler for PATCH /files/:id
handleFileUpdate :: Value -> FileRecord -> Either T.Text FileRecord
handleFileUpdate rawRequest existingFile =
  case parseRequest rawRequest of
    Nothing  -> Left "Invalid request format"
    Just ctx -> 
      let updatedFile = applyUpdate ctx existingFile
      in Right updatedFile

-- Example: simulate processing a request
exampleUsage :: IO ()
exampleUsage = do
  let existingFile = FileRecord
        { fileId = "file-001"
        , fileName = "report.pdf"
        , fileOwner = "alice"
        , fileRole = Editor
        , fileContent = "original content"
        , isPublic = False
        , storageClass = "standard"
        }
  -- A normal editor request from the proxy
  let request = object
        [ "X-User-Role" .= ("editor" :: T.Text)
        , "X-User-Id"   .= ("bob" :: T.Text)
        , "body"        .= object
            [ "fileName" .= ("updated_report.pdf" :: T.Text)
            , "fileContent" .= ("new content" :: T.Text)
            ]
        ]
  case handleFileUpdate request existingFile of
    Left err -> putStrLn $ "Error: " ++ T.unpack err
    Right f  -> print f
